title: HyperGC: Learning Hypergraph Representations via Full Hyperedge Reconstruction and Contrastive Evaluation

problem.claim: Hypergraph representation learning is needed to model complex groupwise relationships in real-world data.

gap.claim: Existing generative self-supervised hypergraph representation learning methods suffer from incomplete high-order semantic capture and unstable, sample-sensitive negative-sampling evaluation.

contributions.claim: HyperGC is a hybrid self-supervised hypergraph representation learning framework that unifies generative and contrastive learning.
The framework performs full hyperedge reconstruction through progressive selection with dynamic target cross-entropy.
The framework uses multi-view contrastive evaluation without handcrafted negative samples.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments cover 11 real-world hypergraph datasets and three tasks: node classification, hyperedge prediction, and community detection.
The authors report that each strategy is effective individually and that their combination consistently achieves the best performance.
The authors report improvements of up to 12.27%, 5.12%, and 34.35% on the respective tasks over 19 state-of-the-art hypergraph representation learning methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Hypergraph representation learning addresses complex groupwise relationships.
Existing generative self-supervised approaches have limitations in full high-order reconstruction and stable evaluation.
HyperGC addresses the limitations with full hyperedge reconstruction and multi-view contrastive evaluation.
Experiments across datasets and tasks report benefits for each strategy and their combination.

source_observation.claim: The reported combination of complementary generative and contrastive strategies performs best across the evaluated tasks.

interpretation.claim: Combining representation learning objectives with evaluation mechanisms that address distinct failure modes may improve robustness across tasks.

application.claim: For self-supervised relational learning systems, pair objectives that improve structural reconstruction with evaluation procedures that reduce dependence on sampled negatives.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this combination generalizes beyond the reported datasets, tasks, or hypergraph setting.

unknowns: Model architecture and implementation details are not specified.
Dataset identities, evaluation protocols, and statistical significance are not reported.
The abstract does not provide per-dataset results or explain the source of the reported percentage improvements.
